sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
This command works (run from `<run>\work\L1\c\w`):

```
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Both tests pass (`test_transfer_preserves_total` and `test_rejects_non_positive_amount`).

Without `PYTHONPATH=src`, the run fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ledgerlite'`. The package sits under `src/` and isn't installed, so Python can't find it. I didn't change any files.

That syntax is for the Bash shell. In PowerShell, use `$env:PYTHONPATH="src"; python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`. In cmd, use `set PYTHONPATH=src && python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`.

actions.command: PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v 2>&1 | tail -15

sessions.name: B
sessions.reply:
I added `Ledger.close(name)` in `src/ledgerlite/__init__.py`. It raises `ValueError` if the account's balance isn't zero, and otherwise removes the account. Closing a name that doesn't exist raises `KeyError`, the same as `balance()` does.

I also added `test_close_requires_zero_balance` in `tests/test_ledger.py`. It checks that closing a non-zero account raises and leaves the account in place. It then checks that the same account closes once its balance is back to zero.

The full suite passes, 3 tests including the new one. It only runs with `src` on the import path:

```
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```
